branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Meeting materials and chair framing reduce alternative discussion time and elevate vendor cost comparisons above reform options.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Undecided board members cohere around outsourcing, workers oppose publicly, and management emphasizes implementation safeguards.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Board packet presents outsourcing as uniquely credible savings path with manageable service-risk claims.

branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Executives are directed to return with in-house savings targets, operational redesign, or quality metrics instead of contract terms.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Board requests internal efficiency plan, performance benchmarks, or pilot reforms while retaining workforce.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Board perceives quality and legitimacy risks from outsourcing as too high relative to uncertain savings.

branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Discussion shifts from contract award to quantified workforce givebacks, job guarantees, or negotiated benchmarks.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Management and board test whether concessions can close enough of the savings gap to defer privatization.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Workers or their advocates signal willingness to accept scheduling, staffing, or compensation concessions to avert outsourcing.

branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Chair or swing members call for additional review, procurement detail, or patient-quality evidence before binding action.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Vote is postponed for further analysis, hearings, or comparative proposals, preserving all main endpoints.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Board members conclude information is incomplete or public backlash risk is rising.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: A delay, in-house reform directive, or labor-concession package could preempt this endpoint without disproving that outsourcing had early momentum.
endpoint_ledger.description: Board authorizes transition of cafeteria services to an external vendor or launches binding procurement/award that commits the hospital to outsourced operation.
endpoint_ledger.label: Outsourcing approved

meta.important_question: Will the hospital board ultimately approve outsourcing cafeteria services rather than retain direct operation?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: This is the most explicit privatization endpoint and a central comparison case for later divergence.
realization_criteria: hospital_board records a majority vote approving outsourced cafeteria operation or binding vendor award
official board minutes/resolution commit the hospital to external operation beyond a temporary study
implementation authority is delegated to management for outsourced transition
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Outsourcing is explicitly named as a live option under budget pressure with vendor lobbying present, but no decision has yet been taken.

blockers: finance estimates showing insufficient internal savings
board belief that management cannot execute reform quickly
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: A temporary study request alone does not realize this endpoint unless the board actually selects internal retention as the path.
endpoint_ledger.description: Board decides to retain cafeteria services internally while requiring operational reform, cost savings, or performance benchmarks.
endpoint_ledger.label: In-house reform adopted

meta.important_question: Will the board commit to an in-house reform path with explicit performance or savings requirements instead of outsourcing?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: This endpoint captures a substantive non-outsourcing resolution rather than mere process delay.
realization_criteria: hospital_board formally rejects outsourcing in favor of internal retention
board resolution or executive directive sets measurable in-house savings, quality, or restructuring targets
no binding external vendor commitment is authorized as the selected terminal model
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Scenario explicitly calls for branch hypotheses around in-house reform, and patient quality concerns make this a credible alternative.

blockers: insufficient concession magnitude relative to savings target
board preference for outsourcing regardless of concessions
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Worker statements of flexibility do not realize this endpoint unless concessions are formalized and recognized as dispositive.
endpoint_ledger.description: The dispute resolves through worker concessions that materially satisfy board/management savings demands and avert outsourcing.
endpoint_ledger.label: Labor concession settlement

meta.important_question: Will worker concessions become the terminal mechanism that resolves the cafeteria governance dispute?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: This endpoint operationalizes a compromise path driven by switching costs and labor dependency.
realization_criteria: cafeteria_workers or recognized representatives accept quantified concessions on compensation, scheduling, staffing, or work rules
hospital_board or management formally states concessions are sufficient to retain in-house operation
outsourcing option is withdrawn or suspended on the basis of the concession package
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Labor concession is explicitly identified in the scenario as a branch option but no organized agreement exists at T0.

blockers: clear majority already favoring one substantive option
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: A short recess within one meeting does not count unless the substantive decision is deferred beyond the initial decision window.
endpoint_ledger.description: Board postpones a binding service-model choice beyond the initial decision window for further study, hearings, or comparative review.
endpoint_ledger.label: Decision delayed

meta.important_question: Will the board postpone a binding decision rather than choose a service model in the near term?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Process delay is not terminal in the long run, but within this scenario's initial endpoint pressure it is a meaningful near-term outcome that preserves all substantive branches.
realization_criteria: hospital_board declines to take a binding vote at the expected decision point
board chair or board resolution schedules additional review, hearings, or analysis before selecting outsourcing or retention path
no terminal service-model commitment is made within the immediate vote window
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Delayed vote is explicitly named as a branch option and is plausible when legitimacy, quality, or data concerns remain unresolved.

risk_flags.note: The corpus does not specify whether cafeteria workers have formal union representation, affecting concession and mobilization pathways.
Public-hospital contracting constraints and procurement law are not described, limiting precision on outsourcing speed and reversibility.
Number of board members, faction balance, and swing votes are not specified, so authority is clear but coalition math is uncertain.
Patient food-quality concern is established, but baseline quality data are missing, making trust shifts conditional on future evidence.
Vendor influence is present but partly hidden; exposure or leak events could sharply alter legitimacy perceptions later.

simulation_brief.summary: A fictionalized public hospital board is approaching a vote on whether to outsource cafeteria services amid budget pressure. Cafeteria workers fear job loss, patients care about food quality, vendors are quietly lobbying, and board members are balancing fiscal, labor, and public-legitimacy concerns. T0 includes unresolved dependencies, mixed public/private stances, and multiple credible endpoint paths: outsourcing, in-house reform, labor concession, or delayed vote.
uncertainty_notes: Exact hospital size, board composition, union status, and vendor identities are unspecified.
Budget pressure is established, but the magnitude of the deficit and procurement constraints are not specified.
Public salience appears moderate at T0 rather than full crisis.

sociology_baseline.evidence: Actors likely update within familiar frames such as budget credibility, service quality, and fairness rather than radical shifts at T0.
Mobilization likely requires visible trigger such as leaked savings plan, testimony, or quality-risk narrative.
Many affected actors have concerns but limited expression at T0.
Workers, staff, and board members each sort information within role-based networks.
Public concern likely spreads only after repeated cues from workers, clinicians, or visible meeting conflict.
Labor, governance, and care identities shape how the same budget facts are interpreted.
Absent a salient incident, outside attention to cafeteria governance remains low.

sociology_prompt_influences.description: Cost-savings framing increases receptivity among fiscally attentive actors but can weaken trust if quality concerns are not addressed.
Concrete worker job-loss narratives can activate fairness concerns and raise public attention.
Any signal that outsourcing may change food quality can expand patient and clinician engagement.
Perceived nontransparent vendor access can increase legitimacy scrutiny even without broad mobilization.
Scheduling a near-term vote versus extending review materially shapes coalition formation and conflict intensity.
